name: Easy Gluten Free Oat Waffles
description: Light, crispy waffles made with oat flour - naturally gluten-free

equipment.notes: Belgian or standard - adjust batter amount accordingly
One for dry, one for wet ingredients
Keeps waffles crispy - don't stack them

ingredients.notes: Use certified gluten-free if needed. Can make by blending rolled oats.
Check expiration - old baking powder won't give good rise
Coconut milk, nut milk, or dairy all work
Can substitute 5 tbsp melted unsalted butter
For the batter - more for serving

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: get out two mixing bowls - one large for dry ingredients, one medium for wet. Have your whisk and measuring cups/spoons ready. Set up a cooling rack near your waffle iron.
prep_steps.notes: Room temperature eggs and milk mix better - take them out now if you haven't

prep_steps.instruction: Measure oat flour, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon into the large mixing bowl. Whisk to combine.
Melt coconut oil (microwave in 20-second intervals or in a small pan)
In the medium bowl, whisk together milk, melted coconut oil, eggs, maple syrup, and vanilla extract
prep_steps.notes: If coconut oil solidifies on contact with cold milk, microwave briefly to re-melt

cook_steps.instruction: Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir with a large spoon until just combined - batter will be slightly lumpy.

cues.visual: No dry flour visible, but some lumps remain

cook_steps.warnings: Don't overmix - this makes tough waffles

cook_steps.instruction: Let batter rest for 10 minutes so oat flour can hydrate
Preheat waffle iron to medium-high setting
Give batter one more gentle stir. Pour enough batter to cover center and most of waffle iron surface. Close lid.

cues.visual: Batter spreads to edges when lid closes

cook_steps.warnings: Amount varies by waffle iron - start with less, adjust

cook_steps.instruction: Cook until waffle is deeply golden and crisp - timing varies by iron, usually 3-5 minutes

cues.visual: Deep golden color, no steam escaping from edges

cook_steps.warnings: Don't open too early - waffle will tear. Wait until steam stops.

cook_steps.instruction: Transfer waffle to cooling rack. Do NOT stack waffles or they'll get soggy.
Repeat with remaining batter. If keeping warm, place rack in 200°F oven.

finishing.instructions: Serve warm with maple syrup and nut butter, fresh berries, sliced banana, or any toppings you like.
finishing.make_ahead: Batter doesn't keep well - make fresh. Cooked waffles can be frozen.
finishing.storage: Freeze cooked waffles in single layer, then transfer to freezer bag. Toast from frozen to reheat.

notes: Room temperature ingredients mix more smoothly and help prevent coconut oil from solidifying
The 10-minute rest is important - oat flour needs time to absorb liquid
For extra crispy waffles, let them cool on the rack for 1 minute before eating
Make your own oat flour by blending rolled oats in a blender until fine
